title: The Story of Bhutan’s UN Membership
gist: A historical piece on Bhutan joining the UN on September 21, 1971, the second-to-last South Asian state to do so, after King Jigme Dorji Wangchuk applied in December 1970 seeking the sovereign equality the UN offers small nations.

insights.claim: Bhutan joined the United Nations on September 21, 1971, making it the second-to-last South Asian state to gain membership, ahead of only Bangladesh.
insights.speaker: Birat Anupam
insights.so_what: Historical context for Bhutan's sovereignty positioning between India and China.

insights.claim: Bhutan's King Jigme Dorji Wangchuk applied for UN membership on December 10, 1970, mainly to obtain the sovereign equality the body offers small nations.
insights.speaker: Birat Anupam
insights.so_what: Illustrates how small states use multilateral membership as a sovereignty hedge against larger neighbors.

insights.claim: India's UN representative Samar Sen addressed the Security Council meeting on Bhutan's admission request in February 1971, reflecting India's role in sponsoring Bhutan's entry.
insights.speaker: Birat Anupam
insights.so_what: Underlines India's historic patronage of Bhutan in multilateral forums.
